mn119:0.2: For the translator’s rendering of Sutta 118—Mindfulness of Breathing see the separate book of that name issued by B.P.S. Kandy.
mn119:2.3: In some places the translator has ‘mindfulness occupied with the body’; it would also be possible to translate ‘mindfulness directed at the body’: in both cases translating ‘gata’ (lit. ‘gone to’).
mn119:7.2:
midriff: This means not only the midriff but all the fascia or tough membranes which bind the various bits and pieces together and keep them in place.

entrails: In Thai these last two are translated ‘large gut, small gut.’

grease: ‘Grease’ means ‘skin-grease’.
mn119:29.1: para. 52. See VisA 248-9 for commentary: sati sati āyatane’ti tasmim tasmim pubbahetu-ādi kāraṇe sati.
